title: clause_template
statement: Clause order: [FRAME] [TOPIC hozi] SUBJECT [TENSE] [noma] [ne] [MODAL] [APPROACH] [PHASE] [EFFORT] [ASPECT] [ITERATION] [EVIDENTIAL] VERB [OBJECT] [ADJUNCTS] [fuyi] [hoyo|yasmo] [ATTITUDE] [ki].

title: slots[3]
statement: The subject is obligatory except in commands, hortatives and permitted ellipsis.

title: slots[4]
statement: Tense is po (past), futu (future) or pressa (present); no tense word = present.

title: one_per_slot
statement: At most one word per operator slot (one modal, one evidential, one tense…).

title: exclusions
statement: Excluded pairs: hiro/teki with roni/tefa; telvo/vazdi/fesmo with tefa; zoke with seye/mufe/poye/pifu; tavki with fututi; hoyo with yasmo.

title: max_preverbal_operators_recommended
statement: No more than four preverbal operators are recommended.

title: slots[6]
statement: ne floats: it may stand before any later operator or the verb, negating what follows.

title: slots[12]
statement: reve and loki may close the clause instead of standing in the iteration slot.

title: slots[1]
statement: FRAME words are clause-initial and followed by a pause (comma).

title: slots[2]
statement: At most one hozi topic per clause, except paired contrastive topics in parallel clauses.

title: slots[20]
statement: ki is the last word of its clause.

title: slots[19]
statement: Attitude words close the clause, before ki; zoke excludes the other four.

title: scope_operators
statement: ne, doli, tu, yesta, pendi, vinto stand immediately before the constituent they scope over.

title: valency
statement: CAUSER [TENSE…] vaku|lesvu|tekvu ACTOR [ne] [APPROACH] [PHASE] [EFFORT] VERB [OBJECT].

title: noun_phrase
statement: Noun phrase: [QUANTIFIER] [li|eli|ola|OWNER de] [NUMBER] [ADJECTIVES] NOUN[-ti][-ri] [de …] [raho CLAUSE].

title: seven_forms
statement: Every headword has seven forms: R, R+asa, R+na, VERB, R+nasan, R+san, R+asasan.

title: verb_rule
statement: Verb: opi→opioa; n-initial R+nia; s-initial R+sia; vowel-initial R+a; otherwise R + first consonant + a.

title: suffix_order
statement: ROOT + (one form OR one derivation) + -ti + -ri; -ri is always last.

title: compounding
statement: MODIFIER+HEAD written together, head rightmost; a compound's verb class follows its first letter.
flags: STALE: the lexicon's text says components must be active 1.0 headwords. 2.0:G38 (colour bases as modifiers), 2.0:G42 (nested compounds) and every compound built on a post-1.0 headword contradict it.

title: derivation_defaults
statement: Default readings: -yo one who does/is devoted to R; -vu big or intense R; -pago place of R; -ti little or dear R; a listed derivation overrides.
flags: STALE: morphology.suffixes still says -yo and -vu attach 'on the root'; 2.0:G41 says derivations attach to any root or compound.

title: -pago
statement: mavo + -pago is blocked: mavopago means society only.

title: motion_prefixes
statement: Motion prefixes va- du- taro- yave- revo- are a closed, non-productive list, on motion verbs and the curated metaphors only.

title: stress
statement: Stress falls on the penultimate syllable; adjacent vowels are separate syllables.

title: new_root_template
statement: New roots: two syllables, consonant-initial, vowel-final, inventory letters, no initial cluster but kr- tr-, no three-consonant cluster, no doubled letter, two edits from every active word.

title: function_word_template
statement: Function words: one to three syllables, vowel-final, no initial cluster, two edits from every active word except declared monosyllable pairs.

title: Source of truth and name
statement: The JSON is authoritative; the workbook is generated. Language field and files are named Liraasa.

title: Predictable unused slots
statement: An unused form may receive a gloss only when its compositional meaning is predictable, approved case by case, and recorded in authorized_changes.

title: Root Review queue
statement: Frozen for 0.8. No canonical root is respelled; the 40-root queue carries forward unchanged.

title: Frame tense
statement: A standalone tense particle opening a paragraph or turn (Po — / Futu —) sets a frame:

title: Article omission
statement: li may be omitted in everyday speech as well as verse when the referent is obvious;
flags: INTERACTION with 1.2:G29: li may be omitted when the referent is obvious, but an adjective may stand as a noun only after a determiner. Whether li can be omitted before an adjective used as a noun is not said.

title: sige
statement: sige clauses never inherit tense; they are always marked. Tense inheritance applies to fime, raho, kube, nayo, kasa, kopisa and tuni.
flags: UNDERSPECIFIED: tense inheritance is listed for fime, raho, kube, nayo, kasa, kopisa, tuni (and kroti/krotiapo by 2.2:G66). kureli (as soon as), sina (unless), si (if) and nevi (although) are not listed either way.

title: Yesterday evening
statement: deyaapo is kept as a fossil (it retains the retired past marker apo).

title: Double -a verbs
statement: amorliraa, amorrinbaa and amorvulraa are correct;

title: ki with certainty
statement: A certainty marker (or zoke) precedes ki:

title: Sacred register
statement: Registers are defined in the grammar guide.

title: Headword target
statement: New vocabulary is sized by genuine gaps, not by the 120-150 target.

title: -ti on names
statement: The diminutive -ti may attach to personal names as an affectionate or teasing form (Dorinti).

title: Demonstratives as pronouns
statement: eli/ola (and eliri/olari) stand alone for things, situations and discourse (ola = what was just said;

title: Negation scope
statement: ne precedes what it negates: verb or modal (after tense), copula (ne ka), noun phrase or fragment (Ne eli), or a contrasted constituent (ne X, nara Y). Negation is compositional: ne + nuna- is a positive (avoid).

title: Ellipsis
statement: Everyday speech may omit a repeated subject in coordinated clauses and in answers, omit a repeated predicate after a contrasting subject (Dorin, ne.), answer with tense + verb (Po sapusia.), and echo a word with ki.

title: Quotation and embedded questions
statement: ki may close the main clause before an appended direct quotation (Taivo desida ki, fime maivo senosia:
flags: CONTRADICTION: the clause left standing after 2.2:G60's partial supersession says embedded yes/no questions use si (whether). 1.0:G2 says si means only 'if' and 'whether' is ki-oro, and 2.2:G60 itself says embedded yes/no questions use ki-oro. The supersession marked only the wh-word clause.

title: Relative time in subordinate clauses
statement: Inside an inheriting clause: tefa marks prior action, nayo/roni simultaneous, futu subsequent (future-in-past), sahi habitual.

title: Nominalization
statement: The root (form 1) is the noun of action or thing (juba, donu, tali).

title: Noun-phrase order
statement: [toda|rada|muya|poka|somi|nuna] [li|eli|ola|OWNER de] [NUMBER] [ADJ...] NOUN[-ti][-ri] [de ...] [raho ...].

title: Sameness, difference, similarity
statement: X ka sambasan ko Y (same as); X ka sambanasan da Y (different from); gase NP alone = like NP (simile); gase ADJ gase NP = as ADJ as NP. Lotero silda, ... = on the other hand.

title: Scope by position
statement: Every preverbal operator scopes over everything to its right.

title: si and whether
statement: si means only 'if'. 'whether' is ki-oro. 0.8 texts that used si for 'whether' are read under 0.8 rules.

title: Permission vs possibility vs ability
statement: povi = ability; nosi = epistemic possibility (might); dagi = permission (may, be allowed). 0.8's double use of nosi is split.

title: Epistemic necessity
statement: 'must (logically)' = inferential evidential tosu + seye;

title: Intention
statement: Intent is the verb chain 'dorvada sidu VERB' (intend to);

title: Counterfactual
statement: noma marks a clause as contrary to fact. 'should have' = po noma suvi; 'could have' = po noma povi; 'would have' = po viki (in a consequence clause) or po noma viki.

title: Imminence
statement: fututi in the approach slot means 'about to':

title: Continuation
statement: loki covers both 'still' and 'keep on'; no separate continuative is added.

title: Quantity limits
statement: Before a number or quantity, lusu = at least, mosa = at most, gase = approximately;
flags: UNDERSPECIFIED: lusu/mosa are 'at least/at most' before a number, but the function-word table glosses them 'least'/'most' (superlatives: mosa vanisan). The two uses are not stated together.

title: Paired conjunctions
statement: oro A oro B = either A or B; ne A ne B = neither A nor B; doli si = only if; yesta si = even if; 'si …, ata doli si …' = if and only if.

title: Despite
statement: nevi + noun phrase = despite: nevi li zeldo, despite the resistance. nevi + clause = although.

title: Benefactive
statement: vobi + noun phrase = for the benefit of / on behalf of (unchanged), and combines with any operator.

title: ata
statement: ata is 'and' only; additive 'also' is tu.

title: Valency operators
statement: vaku (make), lesvu (let) and tekvu (prevent) fill the verb slot of the main clause;

title: Negation and operators
statement: ne before an operator negates the operator;

title: Exclusions
statement: At most one word per slot. hiro/teki do not combine with roni or tefa. tavki excludes fututi (same slot). The effort slot (telvo, vazdi, fesmo) excludes tefa. noma requires a tense, modal or si-clause context.

title: Unexpectedly / previously / simultaneously
statement: la vuzinasan = unexpectedly; kroti ola = previously; nayo ola = meanwhile/simultaneously; krotiapo = subsequently. No new words.

title: Topic and focus together
statement: A hozi-topic opens the clause; vinto may then mark a focus inside it. hozi and vinto never mark the same constituent.

title: Version gating
statement: Texts dated before 1.0 are interpreted with the 0.8 lexicon and rules.
flags: DOC: the guide's 'Reading older texts' list (handoff/Liraasa_2_3_Rulings.md) gives replacements that later editions retired: barni → kupa (now ruko), velbi → vugo (now vizu), volda → larbopagobudi (now farvibudi), nalsi → velbivaye (now vizuvaye), zella → velbilavi (now vizulavi), yulve → yelfateyo (now bojidento), nolmu → folnimege (now folniyumli).

title: Lexicalised derivations
statement: tisebitivu (sword), tibivu (rope), kaldopago (prison) and zeldoyo (rebel) are fixed meanings of regular derivations.

title: Closing a relative clause
statement: A raho-clause that does not end the sentence is closed by a comma in writing and a pause in speech:

title: Attitude words are clause-final only
statement: seye, mufe, poye, pifu and zoke never open a clause.

title: Events taking place
statement: venreva (come) with an event as subject means 'take place, happen':

title: Time words: opening or closing
statement: A time word or time correlative (eli-krono, deyapressa, fututi, ki-krono's answers…) may open its clause or close it.

title: oro, alone and paired
statement: A single oro joins two equal constituents, exactly as ata does:

title: Give-type verbs: where the recipient goes
statement: A verb of giving (give, lend, send, owe, sell, pay, bring, teach, show) takes VERB THEME ala RECIPIENT.
flags: UNDERSPECIFIED: the give-type verbs are named in English only (give, lend, send, owe, sell, pay, bring, teach, show); which Liraasa verbs count is decided by the checker's overlay, not the spec.

title: Which side of de is the owner
statement: In X de Y the owner is Y, read as English "X of Y":

title: -ri after a number or quantifier
statement: After a number or a quantifier the plural -ri is optional:

title: An adjective standing as a noun
statement: An adjective may stand as a noun phrase on its own only after an article or determiner (li, eli, ola, baba):

title: "About" is de
statement: Liraasa has no word for "about / concerning".

title: Commands, address and narrative present
statement: A command has no subject: the clause opens at the verb (slot 3 notes), softened with fisa. A person addressed is a noun phrase set off by commas, at the start or end of the clause. In verse, once the time has been set…

title: Possession precedence
statement: When de joins two candidates for owner, the owner is decided in this order:

title: yuta: the instrument
statement: yuta + noun phrase names the instrument or means of an action:

title: Frequency correlatives
statement: A quantifier joined to krono with a hyphen gives a frequency adverbial:

title: Two more curated motion metaphors
statement: revo-sabesia (know again: recognize) and yave-donuda (give together: share) join revo-vimova and revo-lirala as curated metaphors. The motion prefixes otherwise stay non-productive.

title: Gender in kinship
statement: Kinship words are neutral: purma parent, famli sibling, linu child, purmafamli aunt or uncle. Gender is marked only when it matters, by a compound with minva (female) or tarnu (male) where the lexicon has one (minvali…

title: Two declared one-edit pairs
statement: Declare devo / devi and nevi / devi as permitted one-edit pairs.

title: Colour bases in compounds; compounds lexicalised with -ti
statement: Colour bases may act as the modifier in a dictionary compound, and a compound may be lexicalised with -ti.

title: Gold and silver as headwords
statement: aurumijuba and vanajuba become dictionary headwords as well as colour words.

title: Image compounds
statement: Image compounds: any listed modifier + any listed head is a valid word with a predictable meaning, no 'new' flag needed (see pattern_compounds).

title: Productive derivations
statement: Derivations are fully productive with default readings:

title: Nested compounds
statement: A compound may take a compound as one of its two parts:

title: Consonant values
statement: Vowels are pure, as in Spanish or Italian.

title: Neighbouring vowels in song
statement: Every written vowel is its own syllable (0.8:R8), but in singing neighbouring vowels may glide into one note:

title: Foreign names
statement: A foreign name is not translated. It is copied as closely as Liraasa letters allow, choosing among near spellings by how the name sounds and sings.

title: Questions keep every word in place
statement: A question word stands where its answer would stand;

title: Exclamatives
statement: A main clause with a ki-word and no final ki is an exclamation (!).

title: Blessings and wishes
statement: pifu with any subject is the blessing form:

title: Once and N times
statement: NUMBER-krono = N times (una-krono once, dossa-krono twice);

title: Different-subject complements
statement: A second verb with its own subject goes in a fime clause:

title: Evidentials
statement: No evidential = no claim about source. Inside fime, the evidential reports the main-clause subject's evidence. In a question it asks the listener's source.

title: Relatives on a prepositional object
statement: raho opens the clause; the preposition keeps its place with a resumptive pronoun (ito/itori, saivo/saivori): Li nimu raho maivo po lirala en ito, ka vanisan.

title: Partitive de
statement: After a number, quantifier, or superlative, de means of/among and G27/G32 ownership does not apply:

title: Result clauses
statement: ola-modo + ADJ ... fime CLAUSE = so ADJ that: Taivo ke ola-modo vanisan fime li veluri lasola.
flags: UNDERSPECIFIED: superseded by 2.2:G62, but no ruling says whether the superseded construction (ola-modo + ADJ … fime) is now wrong or merely not preferred. The same question applies to 2.1:G46 and 2.1:G47.

title: Duration, ago, from now
statement: Bare measure after the object = duration;
flags: UNDERSPECIFIED: 'kroti + measure (no article) = ago', but the function-word table's own example of kroti ('before') is 'kroti deya', a bare noun, which reads as 'a day ago' under G55. What counts as a measure is not defined.

title: Prohibitions
statement: ne + command, no subject; fisa softens; yava ne + verb = let us not.
flags: UNDERSPECIFIED: 'yava ne + verb = let us not', but the clause template has no slot for yava (slot 3 only says hortatives may lack a subject).

title: Sound follows meaning
statement: Guidance for new and respelled roots: prefer CVCV; l m n r v for sacred/tender/lyrical; b d g k p t z h for bodily/everyday/harsh; playful b c p for beloved small creatures; related meanings may share a consonant fram…

title: Respelling
statement: A respelled root keeps every meaning and empty slot;

title: Roots replaced by compounds
statement: volda -> larbopagobudi (larbopago + budi);

title: Question-word position
statement: A ki-word may open the clause or stay where its answer would stand;
flags: RESOLVED by 2.3:G76 (2026-10-19): a ki-eli / ki-muya + noun question ends in ki; without ki it is an exclamation.

title: Exclamatives, narrowed
statement: Only ki-modo + adjective, ki-eli + noun and ki-muya + noun make an exclamation, and only when the clause does not end in ki.

title: So … that: tonsi + adjective
statement: tonsi directly before an adjective means “so”;

title: Hopeful purpose: fime + nosi
statement: After a main clause, a fime clause whose verb carries nosi means “in the hope that, so that perhaps”.

title: Headless raho
statement: raho with no noun before it means “the one who, that which”, as subject, object or complement.

title: Adjective + sidu + verb
statement: An adjective may take sidu + verb for “easy to …, ready to …”.

title: kroti and krotiapo before a clause
statement: kroti and krotiapo may introduce a clause:

title: Side nouns as prepositions
statement: nazru (behind), zavme (in front of), silda (beside), cemnu (in the middle of), lizma (left of) and rizno (right of) may stand bare before a noun phrase as prepositions, or after a verb as adverbs.

title: The album as reference corpus
statement: The album (twelve songs and the alternate 05) is canon 2.0 text, read with 2.0 spellings under 2.1:G58.

title: Second respelling pass
statement: Thirteen roots are respelled: lenra -> zarku; vanru -> dokra; voho -> kezdo; vabale -> tobra; teyo -> dento; mege -> yumli; kupa -> ruko; jemla -> zimzi; pesbi -> bondo; menha -> gamdo; vugo -> vizu; salye -> bapi; se…

title: Roots for common animals
statement: bumbo (bear), murmu (cow; cattle) and kerku (frog) are new roots. They replace larbopagoregna, maremirulazu and the listed derivation mirunululirayo, which are retired; kerku takes the verb kerkuka, to croak. mirunulu…
flags: INTERACTION with 2.0:G41: G70 retires mirunululirayo, but G41 makes every R+yo a valid word with a default reading, so mirunululirayo stays buildable ('one devoted to river-song'). The ruling does not say whether a retired listed derivation is still a word.

title: Wolf
statement: larbopagobudi -> farvibudi (farvi + budi), 'wild dog', read like farvilazu (wild animal);

title: A line that continues: ata
statement: ata may open a line or clause that continues the one before, as oro may (1.2:G25):

title: Manner with en and ko
statement: en + an abstract noun names the manner or medium of an act:

title: raho opening a question
statement: A direct question may open with raho for 'who' or 'what' and ends in ki, as the album asks twice (05:22, 11:12).

title: pagopa takes the motion prefixes
statement: pagopa (to go) is a motion verb: the motion prefixes attach to it, as in taro-pagopa, to go across (album 05alt). The prefixes stay a closed list, on the motion verbs and the curated metaphors only (1.2:G35).

title: Questions with ki-eli and ki-muya
statement: A question with ki-eli + noun or ki-muya + noun ends in ki;
